response_sources.constructive_note: Constructive stimuli are derived from each candidate's own rule parameters (keywords, regex samples, length max+1, non-JSON, tool receipts, budget overflow, low retrieval score). They are reported separately from real responses and are not claimed to be LLM output.

real_violation_profile.note: Real chat responses are prose, so format_check / length_bound / token-budget rules fire often; semantic content hits (keyword / pattern / normalized) are rare. This is why L1 still has high audit utility on real responses: the dominant categories map losslessly to repair actions. Constructive stimuli cover the content/tool rules.

settings.classifier: stdlib multinomial naive Bayes (alpha=1); reused from bench_policy_infer.py
settings.l2_primary: actual L2 payload: evidence_commitment tokens + count
settings.l2_count_only: A1 convention: count only, commitments ignored
settings.policy_hash_channel_note: policy.id / policy_hash in the certificate payload are excluded from features by design; a candidate-corpus hash lookup would give top-1 = 1.0 unless policy_nonce is used (BHV theorem D).

trivial_channels.note: not used as attack features; listed to keep the boundary visible

L2 evidence commitments are deterministic SHA-256 of evidence, so the same evidence value is linkable across responses; we therefore include commitments in the L2 feature set (actual payload shape) and also report a count-only A1-style comparison.
